title: How to Use BLS Salary Data Before Your Next Job Offer
description: Free government pay data can tell you what a fair offer looks like. Here is how to read salary percentiles and turn them into a confident ask.
author: MrPress Education Curriculum Team
coverAlt: Abstract illustration of a pay scale with gold and teal markers
body:
When an offer arrives, most people have no idea whether it is fair. The good news: the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes free, reliable pay data for hundreds of occupations every year. Here is how to use it.

## Understand percentiles
BLS reports wages at several points:

- **10th percentile:** 10% of workers earn less than this. Often reflects new workers or lower-paying areas.
- **25th percentile:** A common range for people with a year or two of experience.
- **Median (50th):** Half earn more, half earn less.
- **75th and 90th percentiles:** Experienced workers, specialists and higher-paying employers or regions.

For example, BLS data for May 2025 shows pharmacy technicians earned a median of $45,750, with the 25th percentile at $37,850 and the 75th at $49,990. See the full [pharmacy technician pay scale](/careers/pharmacy-technician/salary/).

## Place yourself on the scale
Ask honestly: Am I new to the field? Do I have a certification employers value? Is this a higher-cost area? A newly certified worker might reasonably target the 25th percentile to the median; an experienced specialist might aim higher.

## Adjust for location
National numbers are a starting point. Pay varies a lot by state and metro area, so compare with local job postings too. Many states and cities now require pay ranges in postings, which makes this easier.

## Turn data into an ask
Use a calm, specific script:

> Thank you for the offer — I’m excited about this role. Based on my certification and pay data for this position, I was hoping for something closer to $48,000. Is there flexibility?

If base pay is fixed, ask about a sign-on bonus, shift differentials, schedule or paid training.

## Find the numbers
Our [salary guide](/salary-guide/) lists BLS pay for 50 careers, and every career has its own salary page with monthly and hourly breakdowns. For more scripts, read [how to negotiate salary](/guides/how-to-negotiate-salary/).
